create.name: Mark V. Wiley
create.bio:
Mark V. Wiley is an author and teacher of embodied practice who began training in martial arts in 1979 and later spent years travelling across Asia, from Manila and Hong Kong to Taiwan and Japan, to learn directly from martial artists, internal-arts practitioners, contemplatives and lineage holders. He also holds degrees in Oriental medicine and medical anthropology. Out of that long apprenticeship he built Inner Life, a framework that brings breath, attention, movement and perception together, with six foundational practices that move from standing stillness into movement, partner work and everyday life.

He teaches mainly online, through one-to-one mentoring on Zoom and through his website's practices, reflections and recorded talks. His YouTube channel, Inner Life with Mark V. Wiley, mixes short teachings with long conversations on meditation, martial arts and wisdom traditions, with guests such as Deng Ming-Dao on the Tao, Shaykh Fadhlalla Haeri on the ego, Michael James on Ramana Maharshi and Brook Ziporyn on freedom in Daoist and Buddhist thought. The talks favour practical questions about how practice changes a person over time.

courses.title: Personal Cultivation Discovery Intensive
courses.description: A 90-minute one-to-one session on Zoom that starts his individual mentoring. He reviews your experience and aims, works through selected movement, breath and attention practices with you, and sets practices to continue.

free_resources.title: The 6 Foundational Practices
free_resources.description: A free, step-by-step sequence of six practices on his site, moving from standing stillness and breath into movement, interaction and presence in action. Each one is meant to be learned before the next.

free_resources.title: Inner Life Talks
free_resources.description: Recorded informal talks and dialogues on practice, attention, structure and embodiment. Free to watch on his site.
